reviewed_by: Delegated coding agent source-semantic review against the live Binary Ninja 6.0.10601 MCP view, Radare2 6.2.0 and angr 10.0.4.post1 CFGFast on retail igi.exe (SHA-256 dea34892...), with the candidate object recompiled for Windows x86.
source_revision: worktree branch 807c1b2d (clean except the pre-existing pyc); implementation bound by engine/src/retail/script/qvm_execute.cpp sha256 17d7ef30330e93850f8187f7abb139cef4162d6964cd530536fed0d7a799d5cf
review_basis: The retail entry was re-read through the live Binary Ninja view, independently recovered by Radare2 and CFGFast, and the candidate object was compiled with the repository -O3 -DNDEBUG flags and disassembled. All branches, calls, stores and returns below were compared instruction by instruction against 0x004B85B0-0x004B86DC.

retail_function.summary: Two mutually exclusive paths, selected by the precompiled-program pointer at qvm+0x8C. Program path: g_a965a4=0, g_a965a8=0, load qvm+0x8C; if non-zero call 0x004BD080(program), store g_a965a4=0, return 0 when it returned 0, otherwise report "Error in QVM program: %s\r\n%s" with (qvm, program+0x268), store g_a965a4=0 and return the reporter's EAX. Source path: 0x004C0200(&var_830,&var_850,&var_800,0x800), 0x004BF1C0(&var_850,qvm[0x80],qvm[0x84]), then loop while (g_a965a0==0 || g_a965a4==0): var_854=0, break when 0x004BFC70(&var_830,&var_828)==0, else if 0x004BF1F0(&var_830,&var_854)!=0 release the block with 0x004BFA80 and 0x004BF8F0 and continue when g_a965a8==0; otherwise report "An error occured in script file: %s" when g_a96598!=0, store g_a965a8=0 and break. Then 0x004BEFC0(&var_850), store g_a965a4=0 and return its EAX.

path_selection.finding: The retail release build executes the precompiled-program path (qvm+0x8C non-zero), not the source parser.
evidence: 0x0040100A: push 1; call 0x0048F330 - Script_SetForcePrecompiledState(1) at the executable's startup stub, before any level load.
0x0048F627: push 1; call 0x0048F1C0 - Script_SetDebugCompileState(1) in main's startup sequence.
0x0048F334 stores the byte argument to 0x005C8BF0 and 0x0048F1C5 stores it to 0x005C8BEC; Qvm_Load (0x004B80B0) reads both through 0x0048F1D0/0x0048F340.
With both flags set, Qvm_Load replaces the extension with .qvm, resolves it through 0x004BD220 and stores the resolved program at qvm+0x8C, so Qvm_Execute takes the 0x004BD080 path.
path_selection.consequence: The source-parsing loop in branch B is the non-precompiled fallback; it contains no opcode dispatch. The instruction loop is Qvm_ExecuteInstructions (0x004BCFD0), reached through 0x004BD080, and is already transcribed separately in qvm_stack_natives.cpp (with an incomplete handler table).

checks.name: function_identity
checks.detail: Binary Ninja, Radare2 and angr all recover the exact entry 0x004B85B0; Binary Ninja names it Qvm_Execute, Radare2 recovers cdecl with one stack argument and 14 blocks/20 edges, and the candidate defines Qvm_Execute as the body implementing that entry.

checks.name: argument_mapping
checks.detail: cdecl with one 4-byte stack argument is preserved. qvm is read once into a register (retail ESI at 0x004B85B7); all field accesses use the retail offsets +0x80, +0x84, +0x8C and program+0x268.

checks.name: branch_structure
checks.detail: The decision order matches: clear both state words, test qvm+0x8C, then the program path or the source path; the source loop tests g_a965a0 first and g_a965a4 second (break only when both are non-zero), breaks on end-of-buffer, and exits through 0x004BEFC0.

checks.name: program_path
checks.detail: 0x004BD080 receives qvm+0x8C; a zero result returns 0; a non-zero result reports the exact retail format at 0x005472BC with (qvm, program+0x268), stores g_a965a4=0 after the call (retail 0x004B8602) and returns the reporter's EAX.

checks.name: source_path
checks.detail: 0x004C0200 receives (&buffer,&stack,text,0x800) in the retail push order; 0x004BF1C0 receives (&stack,qvm[0x80],qvm[0x84]); the parsed slot is zeroed before each 0x004BFC70 call and passed as buffer+0x08; the two block releases run in retail order followed by the g_a965a8 test.

checks.name: error_reporting
checks.detail: Both retail formats are byte-exact, including the retail typo 'occured' and the \r\n between the two program substitutions. The second report is gated on g_a96598 != 0 and is followed by g_a965a8 = 0 in both.

checks.name: return_and_error_paths
checks.detail: Four retail returns: program success returns 0; program error returns Qvm_ReportError's EAX; the source path returns 0x004BEFC0's EAX; every return stores g_a965a4=0 first. The candidate reproduces all four and does not present the source-path value as a script result. Error reporting is gated on g_a96598!=0 for the script path and is unconditional for the program path, exactly as in the retail body.

checks.name: constants_and_offsets
checks.detail: 0x800 arena size, +0x80/+0x84/+0x8C object offsets, +0x268 program error text offset and +0x08 buffer slot are the retail literals. No numeric constant was invented.

checks.name: memory_layout
checks.detail: The 0x20 source stack, 0x30 source buffer and 0x800 text arena are modelled at the retail frame offsets; only pointers to them are passed to callees, so the compiler's different absolute frame placement is not observable. The 0x800 arena stays uninitialised as in retail.

checks.name: shared_state
checks.detail: 0x00A965A4 is defined here and the other three words are declared extern with the retail addresses. The declarations fail closed at link time while qvm_native_loader.cpp keeps them internal; duplicating them here would be silently wrong because Qvm_ReportError sets 0x00A965A8 in its own unit.

checks.name: call_dependencies
checks.detail: All ten retail call sites are declared with their retail cdecl signatures and addresses; none is guessed or replaced by a stub. They are simply not implemented on this branch, which is recorded as a link blocker, not hidden.

checks.name: floating_point_semantics
checks.rationale: Qvm_Execute performs no x87 arithmetic of its own; its only floating-point interaction is through the unported callees, so there is no floating-point semantic to compare at this entry.

checks.name: instruction_loop_and_dispatch
checks.rationale: The retail body contains no opcode dispatch. Binary Ninja's user note calling 0x004B85B0 'the interpreter entry' conflicts with its own callee list: the instruction loop is Qvm_ExecuteInstructions (0x004BCFD0), reached via 0x004BD080. The note is recorded as a conflict, not used as evidence.

checks.name: constants_and_scaling
checks.detail: The only literals are retail literals: 0x800 for the source-text arena passed to 0x004C0200, the QVM object offsets +0x80 (data) and +0x84 (size) and +0x8C (resolved program), the program error-text offset +0x268, and the +0x08 parsed-block out slot inside the 0x30-byte source buffer. No scaling factor, size or bound is invented; the frame sizes 0x20 (source stack), 0x30 (source buffer) and 0x800 (text arena) are asserted with static_assert in the candidate and match the retail frame layout.

checks.name: memory_layout_and_access
checks.detail: All reads are at the retail offsets: qvm+0x80, qvm+0x84, qvm+0x8C and program+0x268. The frame-local objects (0x20 source stack, 0x30 source buffer, 0x800 text arena) are only passed to callees by pointer, so the compiler's different absolute frame placement is not observable; the 0x800 arena stays uninitialised as in retail. The internal field writes performed by the unported callees 0x004C0200 and 0x004BFC70 are not modelled; that is a declared dependency, not a claimed memory-layout equivalence.

checks.name: calls_and_side_effects
checks.detail: The ten retail call sites are reproduced in retail order with the retail arguments: 0x004BD080(program) at 0x004B85D8; 0x004B7E10("Error in QVM program: %s\r\n%s", qvm, program+0x268) at 0x004B85FA; 0x004C0200(&buffer,&stack,text,0x800) at 0x004B8625; 0x004BF1C0(&stack,qvm[0x80],qvm[0x84]) at 0x004B863D; 0x004BFC70(&buffer,&buffer.block_slot) at 0x004B8663; 0x004BF1F0(&buffer,&parsed) at 0x004B8679; 0x004BFA80(parsed) at 0x004B868A; 0x004BF8F0(parsed) at 0x004B8694; 0x004B7E10("An error occured in script file: %s", qvm) at 0x004B86B3; 0x004BEFC0(&stack) at 0x004B86C6. Side effects: g_a965a4=0 at entry, after the program runner, after the program-error report and on every source-path exit; g_a965a8=0 at entry and after a reported script error; g_a965a0 and g_a96598 are read only. The candidate performs no store the retail does not, and none of the callees is replaced by a stub: each is declared with its retail cdecl signature and left unresolved (documented link blocker).

signature_comparison.rationale: Retail is cdecl with one stack argument and returns whatever the selected path leaves in EAX. The candidate is extern "C" __cdecl std::int32_t Qvm_Execute(void* qvm), preserving the argument slot, cdecl cleanup and 32-bit return. humanplayer_defines.cpp declares the same symbol as returning void because HumanPlayer_LoadParameters ignores the result; that is ABI-compatible with this definition and is recorded rather than changed (the file is outside this increment).

limitations: The eight retail callees are declared with their retail cdecl signatures but are not transcribed on this branch; the object therefore does not link, and no execution path past this function can run yet.

0x00A965A0, 0x00A965A8 and 0x00A96598 are still defined inside qvm_native_loader.cpp's anonymous namespace. This unit declares them extern to keep the retail storage shared; until those three definitions move to external linkage the link fails. A duplicate definition here was deliberately not used because it would split the state Qvm_ReportError and Qvm_SetGlobalState update.
No paired retail/candidate runtime capture exists for this address; runtime_tests and behavioral are intentionally null and RUNTIME_TESTED/VERIFIED is not claimed.

Which Qvm_Execute branch the retail takes was established statically, not by a runtime capture: the startup stub calls 0x0048F330(1) at 0x0040100A and main calls 0x0048F1C0(1) at 0x0048F627, so debug-compile and force-precompiled are both 1 and Qvm_Load resolves the .qvm program into qvm+0x8C (branch A). Branch B is the non-precompiled source path.

The retail argument order of 0x004C0200 is (buffer, source_stack, text, 0x800) as pushed at 0x004B8611-0x004B8625; the callee is unported, so its internal field writes are inferred only from its disassembly and are not reproduced here.

The candidate object compiles to 14 blocks/21 edges (Radare2 on the COFF object with relocations applied) against 14/20 in retail; the extra edge is GCC's explicit jump from the source-path tail to the shared return block where retail falls through.
The instruction count is 82 candidate vs 90 retail; byte extent 432 vs 301 including padding, because of GCC register allocation, frame size and epilogue placement.

The pre-existing scripts/GameNatives/qvm/004B85B0-Qvm_Execute.cpp candidate is a raw decompiler dump and was not used: its source-parser error path calls Sys_FreeMemory_22 with the report format string instead of Qvm_ReportError (0x004B7E10), and its signature/return comments repeat the stale 'script result value' claim. This transcription was made from the retail body.
